No, not all of it. Of the 81.3 ha of 2021 tree-cover loss mapped by Hansen (2.23% of the asset), the MGAP 2021 forest map places about 68.1 ha (~84%) in planted forest, specifically Pinus elliottii and Pinus taeda. It places about 13.2 ha (~16%) outside any mapped forest. None falls in native forest (0 ha).

Two caveats:
- Hansen also detected another 37.3 ha of loss in patches under 0.5 ha. These were not counted as events, so they are not in the 81.3 ha and their location relative to the plantation isn't given.
- This shows where the loss occurred, not why. Hansen loss includes any stand replacement, such as plantation harvest, so it doesn't establish deforestation, cause, legality, or compliance.

The loss itself is well supported: the JRC 2020 forest reference agrees on 98% of the event area, and later years were observed.
